title: Batch Normalization — Training and Deployment Use Different Measurements
key_insight: During training, batch normalization uses batch mean and variance while updating running estimates. During evaluation, it uses those saved running estimates.
body:
## Training and Deployment Use Different Measurements

A deployed model receives one example, so it cannot depend on a fresh, trustworthy batch average every time.

During training, batch normalization uses batch mean and variance while updating running estimates. During evaluation, it uses those saved running estimates.

Switch model modes correctly. Leaving a model in training mode makes predictions depend on the other examples that happen to share the batch.
common_mistakes: Batch normalization removes every learned parameter.
Evaluation should always use random batch measurements.
Normalization guarantees that overfitting cannot occur.
mini_exercise: Sketch the situation in “Training and Deployment Use Different Measurements” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Stable activation scales can allow faster, less fragile deep-network training.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Training and Deployment Use Different Measurements” situation, explain Batch Normalization without assuming the listener knows deep learning.
